One point, one search, one credit

Eagle Eye pricing is simple: every plan is a bucket of credits, and a scan spends one credit per grid point. A 9 × 9 scan is 81 credits; a 21 × 21 scan is 441. Points you switch off or cut outside a shape cost nothing, and a scan that can’t start is refunded. Credits you buy never expire. A new organisation starts with 10 free scans, and your first scan of your own website is free at any size up to 21 × 21. Set a grid and a rhythm below to see the cost and the plan that fits.

Three numbers, every scan

Three numbers a client remembers and a trend that proves your work paid off. Every scan rolls the whole grid into them — no spreadsheet, no hand-waving.

Local Share of Voice
LSOVLocal Share of Voice

How much of the whole grid finds the business near the top — one number for the entire map.

Average Rank, found
ARPAverage Rank, found

The mean position across only the points that return the business at all.

Average Total Rank
ATRPAverage Total Rank

The same average, counting every point that missed the business entirely — the honest one.

Questions, answered

How does Eagle Eye pricing work?

Every plan is a bucket of credits and a scan spends one credit per grid point: 81 credits for a 9 × 9 scan, up to 441 for a 21 × 21. Points you switch off or leave outside your shape cost nothing, and credits you buy never expire.

Do credits expire?

No. Credits you buy never expire, so a quiet month is never wasted.

Is there a free trial?

A new organisation starts with 10 free scans, and your first scan of your own website is free at any size up to 21 × 21 — no card needed.

What happens if a scan can’t run?

A scan that can’t start is refunded, and points you switch off or leave outside your shape are never charged.

How many plans are there?

Eight, from Starter at $24.99/mo to Enterprise 4 at $4,999/mo — all the same credits, so the plan only sets how many points you can scan.
